title: Even temporal goods: Salazar’s householder analogy—Mary holds the keys of worldly expenses
source_text: LXXI. Neque id tantum de bonis spiritualibus intelligi volunt, sed etiam de temporalibus. Sic enim idem Salazar ea de re Philosophatur, solent, inquit, viri generosi & uxorum amantes, eisdemque plurimum fidentes, pecuniae claves & tutelam eis committere, & quicquid domesticarum expensarum est eis tradere: ipsi vero aliis gravioribus muneribus vacant. Ergo ad eundem modum Deus Opt. Max. sanctissimae sponsae suae Mariae tantundem tribuit, ac fidit, ut ipsi temporalium bonorum tutelam, & claves dederit; adeo ut quicquid horum bonorum, in hac magna mundi domo expenditur, id per Mariae manus recensitum transeat, illius arbitrio distribuatur.
pass_a_gloss: Nor do they wish that to be understood only of spiritual goods, but also of temporal ones. For thus the same Salazar philosophizes on that matter: generous men and lovers of their wives, and trusting them much, are accustomed, he says, to commit to them the keys and guardianship of money, and to hand over to them whatever belongs to domestic expenses: but they themselves are free for other weightier offices. Therefore in the same way God Most High has granted and trusts so much to His most holy spouse Mary that He has given her the guardianship and keys of temporal goods; so that whatever of these goods is expended in this great house of the world passes reviewed through Mary’s hands and is distributed by her choice.
pass_b_english: Not only spiritual goods: Salazar compares Mary to a trusted wife holding the household keys.
God gives her guardianship of temporal goods—worldly outlays pass through her hands.

choices.english: guardianship and keys of temporal goods
choices.why: Extends Marian dispensation to temporal goods.
